title: 7 משחקי קופסא שיעזרו להם לספור ולזהות מספרים

stage.need: Counting and recognising written numbers. CDC lists 'Counts to 10' and 'Names some numbers between 1 and 5 when you point to them' among the 5 year milestones. Board and card games with dice, numbered squares, number cards and play money give that counting a reason: Ramani and Siegler (2008) found that about an hour on a linear number board game raised preschoolers' counting and numeral identification.
stage.age_caveat: Milestones describe what most children do by an age, not a deadline. Some 5 year olds count well past 10 and some need more time; the caption says יש ילדים ש... and each game carries its official age (two of the six are 6+, the top of the range).

dev_sources.title: Milestones by 5 Years
dev_sources.publisher: CDC, Learn the Signs. Act Early.
dev_sources.quote: Counts to 10 / Names some numbers between 1 and 5 when you point to them / Teach your child to follow rules in games. For example, play simple board games, card games, or Simon Says.
dev_sources.supports: 5 year cognitive milestones (counts to 10; names some numbers between 1 and 5) and the tip to play simple board games and card games. Read today through a page fetch (the CDC site blocks plain curl); the three sentences are quoted as returned, joined with ' / '. The page has no tip about counting games, so the link between games and counting rests on the second source.

dev_sources.title: Promoting broad and stable improvements in low-income children's numerical knowledge through playing number board games
dev_sources.publisher: Ramani & Siegler, Child Development 2008;79(2):375-94, doi:10.1111/j.1467-8624.2007.01131.x (PubMed, NIH)
dev_sources.quote: playing such a game for roughly 1 hr increased low-income preschoolers' (mean age = 5.4 years) proficiency on 4 diverse numerical tasks: numerical magnitude comparison, number line estimation, counting, and numeral identification. / Classmates who played an identical game, except for the squares varying in color rather than number, did not improve on any measure.
dev_sources.supports: Peer reviewed, preschoolers with a mean age of 5.4: about an hour on a linear number board game raised counting, numeral identification and magnitude comparison, and a colour version of the same game did not. Limits: low-income preschoolers, a 1 to 10 linear board, and only the abstract was read (PubMed's own page returned a cookie notice, so the abstract text came from NCBI's abstract service for PMID 18366429). It supports 'number board games give counting practice', not a result from any product here; the slides say practise or help, never a promised outcome.

claims.wording_he: משחקי קופסא שיעזרו להם לספור ולזהות מספרים
claims.supports: Ramani and Siegler 2008: about an hour on a number board game raised preschoolers' counting and numeral identification (mean age 5.4); CDC 5 years: counts to 10, names some numbers. 'Can help' only: the study used one linear 1 to 10 board game, not these products.

claims.wording_he: בגיל 5 הרבה ילדים כבר סופרים עד 10
claims.supports: CDC 5 year cognitive milestone: 'Counts to 10' (a milestone most children reach by that age; the caption says some need more time).

claims.wording_he: משחקים עם קובייה קלפים ומספרים מאפשרים להם לתרגל את זה
claims.supports: Ramani and Siegler 2008: playing a number board game gave counting practice that showed on four numerical tasks; CDC suggests simple board games and card games at this age. Written as an opportunity to practise, not a result.

Kodkod's page: money values of 1 to 5 suited to young children; players pay and collect. Counting small amounts is practice of the CDC 5 year counting milestone; our reading, not a tested effect of this game.

The game is built on runs of consecutive number tiles (Center Toys page: runs or groups). Ordering numerals draws on naming numbers (CDC 5 years) and numeral identification (Ramani and Siegler); our reading.

claims.wording_he: מתרגלים לספור צעדים על לוח ממוספר
claims.supports: Kodkod: reach square 100 with an exact number of steps. The closest product tonight to the number board game in Ramani and Siegler 2008 (theirs was linear, 1 to 10).
Fox Mind's page: the game gives practice in telling apart and matching colours and digits. Naming numbers 1 to 5 is a CDC 5 year milestone.

claims.wording_he: מתרגלים לזהות את המספר שעל כל קלף
claims.supports: Cards are matched by number or colour, so the numeral on each card is read every turn. CDC 5 years: names some numbers; suggests simple card games. Reading numerals only, no counting claim.

Fox Mind's page: a game of memory and luck with a little arithmetic, the lowest total wins; skills listed include command of numbers and memory. Magnitude comparison is one of the tasks in Ramani and Siegler 2008. Adding is beyond the 5 year milestones, in line with the game's 6+.

notes: Games research on 2026-10-13 (the run was drawn on 2026-10-12 at 22:06 and the reading happened after midnight, so every accessed date is 2026-10-13, the real day the pages were read). Stage: early_numeracy, ages 5 to 6 (blocked skills and stage ids avoided; same age range as the previous games carousel, a warning). Chosen over memory, language and fine motor because six different kinds of number play were found in Israeli shops and CDC plus a peer reviewed study support it. Toys R Us Israel best-selling sort read in full (463 products, 12 pages of 40 and a last page; the store lists in-stock products first inside each page, so positions are exact to the page only). None of the six is in the top 20 or top 10 percent, so every popular_in_israel label rests on supporting signals from different groups; Triomino Junior (370) and the Ludo board (261) are the thinnest. Makers repeat: three Kodkod products and two Fox Mind products, both also used in the last 14 days (reviewer warnings); Israeli number games for this age are mostly from these two publishers. Rejected: מונופול ג'וניור (same kind as מונופול צעיר, and Kodkod's own Monopoly page lists צעיר), בינגו בורר הקסם (453rd, Kodkod again), ליגרטו ג'וניור (matches colours and pictures, not numbers), שלוף 7 and שיגעון 49 (no official age found, older players), דומינו (out of stock at Toys R Us). Kids and Dragons returned 'too many requests' so it was not used; Amigo's search failed for two terms. LumeBook: the catalogue's counting book (28) is for ages 1-2, so book 86 (Hanukkah, ages 3-10) was used because its story has the child counting candles; it is a holiday book about two months before Hanukkah, which Yarin may want to swap. The book's site page mentions the technology used to make the pictures; nothing of that is in the copy.
